summary: Round 2 re-review of all 9 units. I recomputed every numeric key and worked example (respiratory rates 44 and 66, paracetamol 180 mg, dexamethasone 2.46 mg, ORS 400 mL and 175 mL/h, Holliday-Segar 1400 and 1580 mL, 160 mL and 200 mL boluses, lorazepam 1.5 mg, DKA insulin 1.5 units/h and 9 units over 6 h, PEF 42% and 37.5%, Qp:Qs 1.5 and 3, delays 5.75 and 10.75 h, weight loss 9.7%, 6.3% and 12.5%, z-score -2, MPH 163.5, corrected age 11.5 months and 42 weeks, feeds 510 and 630 mL, herd immunity 83.3%, bilirubin 6 and 8 micromol/L/h, heart rates 90 and 130, Apgar 4, benzylpenicillin 140 and 180 mg/day); all keys are correct and each MCQ has exactly one correct option. Round 1 fixes are in place for isotonic IV fluids and hyponatraemia, BSPED insulin 0.05 units/kg/h, neonatal penicillin age, levetiracetam maximum, dehydration percentages and the worked corrected-age example. Remaining problems: the IM adrenaline age bands still mix BNFc-style bands with an RCUK label, the new UK immunisation table is already out of date (MMRV from 2026) and is incomplete, one corrected-age sentence still contradicts the RCPCH rule, and a few NICE thresholds are dated or unverified. This is an AI review only; the course still needs a subject-matter expert (paediatrician) before clinical reliance, and every dose and schedule here should be source-checked against BNFc, RCUK, BSPED, NICE and the UKHSA Green Book.

issues.problem: IM adrenaline bands are attributed to 'Resuscitation Council UK' but follow BNFc-style bands: 'under 6 months 150 micrograms; 6 months to 5 years 150; 6 to 11 years 300; 12 years and over 500', and '300 micrograms is acceptable if small or prepubertal'. As I recall RCUK (2021 anaphylaxis guideline): under 6 months 100 to 150 micrograms; 6 months to 6 years 150; 6 to 12 years 300; over 12 years 500. The boundaries therefore differ (6 vs 5 years; 11 vs 12 years), so a 12-year-old gets 300 micrograms by RCUK but 500 by the stated bands. Same text is in the lesson paragraph, the table caption and q010's marking guide. I could not check the live documents, so exact current wording is unverified. The 6-11 boundary and the 150 microgram under-6-month dose are consistent with BNFc as I know it but not with RCUK as labelled.
issues.suggestedFix: Verify against the current RCUK and BNFc pages and state one source with its exact bands (and say which source), or present both. If RCUK: under 6 months 100 to 150 micrograms (0.1 to 0.15 mL), 6 months to 6 years 150, 6 to 12 years 300, over 12 years 500. If BNFc: under 6 months 150, 6 months to 5 years 150, 6 to 11 years 300, 12 to 17 years 500 (300 if small or prepubertal). Remove the RCUK label if BNFc bands are used. Source check required.

issues.problem: The new UK schedule table appears outdated and internally inconsistent. The 3 years 4 months row lists 'second MMR-containing dose', but the UK moved to MMRV at 12 and 18 months from 1 January 2026 (so the second dose is no longer a 3y4m item for current cohorts); the 1-year row says the second dose is 'in the pre-school years'. The table also omits the Hib/MenC booster that was in the 1-year visit before the mid-2025 changes and any 18-month visit (I recall changes at 18 months from 2025 to 2026, including an extra hexavalent dose, but this is unverified). Routine annual nasal influenza vaccine in children is not mentioned although listed as a live vaccine. The 8, 12, 16 week rows (6-in-1, MenB, rotavirus, PCV), the 3y4m 4-in-1 booster and the adolescent HPV (single dose), Td/IPV and MenACWY rows match my knowledge. The live-vaccine 'interval rule' (give together or 4 weeks apart) is stated without noting that rotavirus and nasal flu are exceptions. No question tests the schedule although the objective is 'principles of immunisation schedules'.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the table against the current Green Book/NHS schedule: MMRV at 12 and 18 months from 2026 (with the transition for older cohorts), remove or qualify the 3y4m MMR entry, check the 1-year and 18-month visits (Hib/MenC, any hexavalent dose), add annual child nasal flu, and note that MenB/PCV timings and this table need a date stamp. Qualify the 4-week live-vaccine rule. Optionally add one question on the schedule or narrow the objective.

issues.problem: The growth-chart paragraph still says 'use corrected age for infants born before 37 weeks until at least 2 years', contradicting the later RCPCH rule in the same lesson (1 year if born at 32 to 36 weeks, 2 years if before 32 weeks).
issues.suggestedFix: Change the earlier sentence to the RCPCH rule: correct until 1 year if born at 32 to 36 weeks and until 2 years if born before 32 weeks.

issues.problem: Unverified chart values. The hook says a 7.2 kg 9-month-old boy 'sits on the 9th centile'; on WHO boys' data 7.2 kg at 9 months is about -2 SD (roughly the 2nd to 3rd centile). q009 says 8.1 kg at 12 months is 'below the 2nd centile' from the 50th; for a boy that is about the 5th centile (-2 SD is about 7.7 kg), for a girl about the 25th to 50th centile.
issues.suggestedFix: Check against UK-WHO charts and adjust the weights or the stated centiles (or say 'around the 2nd to 9th centile'); state sex in q009.

issues.problem: Bronchiolitis oxygen and admission threshold is given as saturation 'below 92% in air' throughout (lesson, q006, q007). My recollection is that NICE NG9 was updated (2021) to persistent saturation below 90% in babies aged 6 weeks and over without underlying conditions, with 92% retained for under 6 weeks or those with underlying conditions; unverified.
issues.suggestedFix: Check NICE NG9 current text and state the age/comorbidity-specific thresholds (90% vs 92%); q007 (32-week prem, 3 months, sat 90%, severe distress) still justifies admission.

issues.problem: The lesson says 'in a child under 3 years use a urine dipstick' and the q008 marking guide lists 'urine ... for dipstick and culture' for a 6-week-old. As I recall NICE NG224 (2022), dipstick is not recommended under 3 months; those infants need urine culture (and are managed as febrile infants). Unverified.
issues.suggestedFix: State that the dipstick strategy applies to 3 months to 3 years, and that under 3 months a urine sample is sent for culture (check NG224).

issues.problem: Unchanged from round 1. Worked example 'Recording a conversation and a delay' describes a 'swollen forearm' but the X-ray shows a 'spiral humeral fracture' (humerus is the upper arm). Also 'Follow a telephone referral with a written one, usually within 24 hours': Working Together asks for written confirmation within 48 hours, unverified.
issues.suggestedFix: Change 'forearm' to 'upper arm'. Verify the written-referral timeframe against current Working Together guidance and local policy (48 hours as I recall).
